title.narrative: Reviving Agricultural TVET in Ghana by integrating Farm Institutions (Fl's) in the wider agricultural education system with public agricultural colleges and universities

description.narrative:
**Objective**
End hunger and children's undernourishment, double smallholder productivity and income, and ensure the sustainability and resilience of food production systems by 2030 (SDG 2)
**Long-term impact**
End hunger and children's undernourishment, double smallholder productivity and income, and ensure the sustainability and resilience of food production systems by 2030 (SDG 2)
**Outcome(s) at project level**
ATVET/HE organizations (In Ghana and in NL) perform better their core tasks, firmly embedded in their environment (in line with Ghanaian/ regional specific labour market needs & aiming at marginalized inclusiveness and gender mainstreaming).
The following proposed outputs will contribute directly to achieving the project outcomes: - The Farm Institutes offer gender sensitive CBET education by certified teachers - The Farm Institutes implement COTVET accredited new and revised demand-driven, and industry led curricula that are gender sensitive - The Farm Institutes possess the organizational and infrastructural capacity to implement the new and revised curricula - Entrepreneurship capacity of the Farm Institutes enhanced (for students and the tutors)

Farm Institutes’ staff and management, Ghanaian students of Farm Institutes, Ghanaian student about to start agro start-ups, practicing (small holder) farmers, Dutch TVET students, (too limited extent) management of Co

comment.narrative: 09-10-2023: The remaining 4-curriclum packages for the one-year FI program were finalized and accredited by CTVET. A total of 16 courses are finalized: 4 curricula learning materials finished and submitted to CTVET. 12 short courses have also been developed out of the 6 total approved and accredited curricula.

17-02-2023: 2 curricula accredited by CTVET. 4 curricula learning materials finished and submitted to CTVET.
1 cocoa short course is developed – still to be tailored - in collaboration with the OKP TMT project by Kwadaso and Kumasi Technical University and by involvement of FI staff. 1 short-course has been developed in Y3 in collaboration with the GrEEn project with SNV.

20-10-2021: In Year 1, occupational standards have been developed and are validated by COTVET for the following educational programs: - Livestock and Meat Production - Agribusiness - Mechanization and Irrigation - Tree Crop Production - Arable Crop - Poultry Value Chain
In year 2, the focus has been on the development of learning materials for these courses. These will be accredited by COTVET in year 3. After that, additional courses can be developed. Across all the years, at least 12 short courses and/or curricula will be developed whereas the total target for the project is 10.
Tailor made short courses are under development

24-11-2020: In June 2020, occupational standards have been developed and are validated by COTVET for the following educational programs: - Livestock and Meat Production - Agribusiness - Mechanization and Irrigation - Tree Crop Production - Arable Crop - Poultry Value Chain.
The DACUM workshops and Validation workshops had to be re-designed in online workshops, which required more time than the originally planned face-to-face workshops. The curriculum development steps were therefore delayed. Now that the occupational standards are validated by COTVET, the final curriculum development phase can start.
Tailor made short courses are under development
For 6 short courses accreditation is in its final stages.

title.narrative: A.E.3. Number of staff that have gained qualitative and relevant knowledge and skills to develop and offer the revised/developed study programmes

comment.narrative:
09-10-2023: There have been several trainings during the final project year. 123 participants of which 87 males an 36 females trained. Staff has been trained before and can thus not be include in the quantitative section.
The following were achieved in the corresponding trainings and workshops: -16 staff in Poultry curriculum implementation training - 12 in Arable Crops curriculum implementation training - 12 in Tree Crops curriculum implementation training - 14 in Agribusiness curriculum implementation training - 12 staff participated in moodle platform usage and management training 9 – participated in marketing and branding workshop to draw strategies and action plans for targeting potential students and minority groups. - 24 staff members participated in making the business case workshop. - 24 staff members had participated in the development of 12 short courses in the areas of Cocoa, Arable crops production, poultry, livestock, mechanization and agribusiness.
In the indicator section of the 'outcome at project level' 50 staff are mentioned, of which 25% female

17-02-2023: Training for accreditation and registration for 30 FI staff in CBT by CTVET to qualify them for implementation of the revised Diploma curriculum.
Also, 15 FI staff were also involved in the strategic planning workshops, development of cocoa short course on the Cocoa TMT workshop in July 2022.
Again, 15 FI staff were also involved in the development of Learning Materials, Assessment, re-assessment and marking guidelines for the new curriculum that were submitted to CTVET for assessment.

20-10-2021: Curriculum development is clearly progressing( see report 1) (Re-)assessment guidelines need to be completed Learning materials are being developed with all the partners and beneficiaries for all curricula, to be accredited by COTVET in year 3. Composition trainees: 35 male, 25 females. 54 teaching staff, 6 admin staff. Type of program: 1-2 yeas certificate II program (TVET)

24-11-2020: Curriculum development has been almost realized. Only during/after implementation, staff training can start. This has been delayed because of Covid-19. Training in Occupational Standards has been realized.
Face-to-face CBET teacher trainings are delayed because of the inability to travel for international CBET experts. Because of the rural location of the farm institutes, we deem it impossible to re-design the CBET training to online training

24-11-2020: Online learning and communication facilities improved. Further strengthening required. Online training has been introduced, not previously existing.

title.narrative: A.S.4. Number of SMEs supported

comment.narrative: 09-10-2023: In year 2 and 3, each Farm Institute is accommodating Poultry and Catfish Production. Additional: Asuansi FI: Hatchery. Adidome FI: Agro processing. Wenchi: Vegetables Production. This has led to a number of students starting their own small businesses by making use of the F.I’s facilities and later investing in their own facilities.

17-02-2023: Each Farm Institute is accommodating Poultry and Catfish Production. Additional: Asuansi FI: Hatchery. Adidome FI: Agro processing. Wenchi: Vegetables Production. This has led to a number of students starting their own small businesses by making use of the F.I’s facilities and later investing in their own facilities.

For year 2, there are possibilities to support the SME’s in overcoming the challenges due to the COVID outbreak. Financial support for income generating activities at the FI’s will be allocated in Q3 of 2020
